title: The Three Questions
text:
A king decided that he would never fail at anything if he knew three things: the right time to begin each task, the right people to listen to, and the most important thing to do. Learned men gave him conflicting answers, so he went in plain clothes to a hermit known for his wisdom.

The hermit was digging his garden beds and did not answer. Seeing that he was old and tired, the king took the spade and dug for him. Toward evening a bearded man ran out of the woods, holding his stomach, bleeding badly, and collapsed. The king washed and bandaged the wound and spent the night caring for him.

In the morning the stranger begged forgiveness. He was the king's enemy: the king had executed his brother and seized his property. He had come to ambush the king on his way back, and when the king did not return he had been recognized and wounded by the bodyguards. Now the king had saved his life. The king forgave him gladly and promised to return his property.

The hermit then gave the answers. The most important time is now, the only time we have power over. The most important person is whoever you are with. The most important task is to do that person good.
lesson: Long plans are useful, but you only ever act in the present, with the person in front of you. Give them your full attention and help, and many future problems will never arise.
people: A king, a hermit, a wounded man
